_comment: AI driver archetypes. Every trait is 0..1 and they are deliberately
independent — a driver can be committed and inconsistent (fast, crashes)
or cautious and precise (slow, always finishes).
pace_ceiling is the important one for field variety: it caps how fast a
driver goes regardless of what they turned up in. Without it, handing a
nervous club driver a Group B car turns them into a works driver, which
is not how any of this works.
'weight' biases selection: high-skill events field more of the good ones.
'skill_range' is the event ai_skill band an archetype shows up in.

drivers.name: Sunday Driver
drivers.description: Turned up because entry was cheap. Brakes for everything, never uses the road, and will not be troubling the podium.

drivers.name: Nervous Novice
drivers.description: Quick in a straight line, terrified everywhere else. Lifts mid-corner, which is exactly the wrong moment.

drivers.name: Reckless Local
drivers.description: Absolutely committed, absolutely no judgement. Fast until the moment they are not.

drivers.name: Steady Privateer
drivers.description: Pays for the car themselves and drives like it. Never quick, never in the barriers.

drivers.name: Old Hand
drivers.description: Not as quick as they were, but knows every corner and never wastes a metre of road.

drivers.name: Young Charger
drivers.description: Enormous pace, patchy judgement. Will either win or be in a ditch by the second corner.

drivers.name: Works Driver
drivers.description: Paid to do this. Fast, repeatable, and brings the car home.

drivers.name: Gravel Specialist
drivers.description: Grew up sideways on forest roads. Loose surfaces only; put them on tarmac and it shows.
